policy: Original acoustic evidence is not a photo key. Dated forest records cannot be generalized into local occupancy or current population. Distinguish source date, type and locality.

records.label: Comparative snout and male size
records.text: A specimen-based 2008 character table records a vertical snout profile, exposed tympanum and maximum measured male snout–vent length of 19.9 mm for P. albotaeniata.
records.sourceLocation: Table 3, printed p. 441, P. albotaeniata column; examined FMNH specimens listed on p. 443
records.studyScope: Specimen-based comparative summary in a paper about two Bornean species. Snout and size traits do not alone diagnose all Philippine Pelophryne; dorsolateral stripes are variable.

records.label: Male-call comparison with L. beloncioi
records.text: In a 2021 comparative series of four Palawan males, L. acanthi advertisement-call notes contain two pulses, versus one in the Mindoro–Semirara sister species L. beloncioi.
records.sourceLocation: Diagnosis of L. beloncioi; Table 4, Palawan L. acanthi male calls (n=4)
records.studyScope: Acoustic differential in sampled populations, not a visual identification criterion. The authors state external morphology cannot reliably separate the species; island names are not diagnostic by themselves.

records.label: Original advertisement-call series
records.text: The original species description records a Kwek-Kwek advertisement call, sometimes a single note and sometimes a short sequence of two to five notes.
records.source: Brown, Alcala, Diesmos & Alcala (1997), Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 50(1):1–20
records.studyScope: Original study's small recorded call series (n=2); onomatopoeia alone cannot prove species identity. Numeric frequencies not transcribed from OCR.

records.label: Original advertisement-call series
records.text: The 1997 original comparison describes a repeated Tut-Tut-Tut advertisement call with roughly six to twenty-four successive notes in sampled P. banahao males.
records.source: Brown, Alcala, Diesmos & Alcala (1997), Proceedings of the California Academy of Sciences 50(1):1–20
records.studyScope: Recorded sample size n=4; not a sound classifier, not a claim that every male gives the full reported number of notes.

records.label: 2026 upland camera-trap microhabitat
records.text: An Indigenous-led Mindoro camera-trap survey recorded one Mindoro Bleeding-heart in forest above 900 m on 1 August 2026, beyond its commonly cited lower-elevation records.
records.source: Center for Conservation Innovations Philippines (2026), Mindoro Bleeding-heart rediscovery notice
records.sourceLocation: 3 September 2026 announcement; Iraya Mangyan forest monitoring project
records.studyScope: Single confirmed photographed bird in one upland forest location. This is not a full habitat-range shift, abundance estimate or public release of sensitive coordinates.

records.label: Remaining forest survey need
records.text: The September 2026 rediscovery team identified protection and restoration of Mindoro's remaining forests as priorities after its single 2026 camera-trap record.
records.source: Center for Conservation Innovations Philippines (2026), Mindoro Bleeding-heart rediscovery notice
records.studyScope: Conservation-team recommendation and documented finding, not a species-wide threat-rate model or government protection order.

records.label: Camera-detected Palawan habitat types
records.text: A 2016 baited camera-trap study photographed Palawan Pangolin three times at two Palawan localities, reporting mangrove, lowland-forest and riverine-forest settings.
records.sourceLocation: Abstract and Results, two baited sampling localities
records.studyScope: Three photographs do not prove three individuals, population density or unbaited habitat preference. No precise sensitive coordinates are imported.

records.label: Historical forest-range contraction
records.text: The IUCN wild-pig specialist account describes former primary and secondary forest use from lowland to about 1,600 m, with remaining populations mostly in isolated higher-elevation forests after lowland forest loss.
records.source: IUCN SSC Wild Pig Specialist Group, Sus cebifrons detailed account
records.studyScope: Specialist summary is not an independently surveyed elevation threshold. The account cautions that some altered-habitat reports may involve feral pigs or hybrids.

records.label: Hunting and hybridization threats
records.text: The specialist account identifies hunting, habitat loss and possible hybridization with domestic pigs as threats to fragmented Visayan Warty Pig populations.
records.source: IUCN SSC Wild Pig Specialist Group, Sus cebifrons detailed account
records.studyScope: Threats in a specialist account, not a quantified population trend or a new 2026 IUCN status reassessment.
